thesis: A single-vehicle DUI is the likely proximate cause of loss; the repair shop's unverified 'stuck throttle' remark does not support a manufacturer subrogation theory.

supporting_evidence.quote: the throttle pedal feels stuck when pressed. Could be a recall issue, have seen similar on this model.
supporting_evidence.claim: The only potential third-party theory — a manufacturer defect — and it is an unverified repair-shop hypothesis.

contradicting_evidence.quote: Officer Singh observed slurred speech, odor of alcohol on driver's breath.
contradicting_evidence.claim: Officer's contemporaneous observations point to driver impairment as the cause.
The driver was cited for DUI, an intervening cause that likely bars recovery.

contradicting_evidence.quote: Romero refused field sobriety at scene.
contradicting_evidence.claim: Refusal of field sobriety testing further supports the impairment theory.

estimated_recovery_basis: No recoverable third-party theory is established; the manufacturer-defect angle is unverified and speculative.
open_questions: The BAC result is still pending from the San Mateo County blood draw.
The NHTSA recall database has not yet been checked for this model.
The repair shop's stuck-throttle observation needs independent inspection.
reviewer_warnings: Single-vehicle DUI is an intervening cause that likely bars subrogation against a manufacturer in CA.
The manufacturer-defect angle is speculative — a repair-shop hypothesis with no NHTSA verification.
Do not name Toyota as a recovery target on this record.
